articles.summary: Citing an MIT finding that 95% of gen AI projects fail and a National Bureau of Economic Research survey where 90% of executives saw no measurable productivity gain from AI, De Cremer argues leaders keep framing AI as a quick fix for urgent bottlenecks rather than a tool for durable value creation. He recommends prioritizing clarity of purpose and resisting urgency bias over chasing fast wins.
articles.tieback: Applied to supply chain, the durable value comes from automating the underlying vendor onboarding and EDI plumbing rather than bolting AI onto processes that are still manual and disconnected underneath.

articles.title: Visa and BBVA Prove Today's Rails Can Handle Agentic Payments
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: BBVA completed its first AI agent-initiated payment transaction in partnership with Visa, using real card credentials under the Visa Agentic Ready program in Europe. The transaction relied on tokenization, real-time fraud monitoring and biometric authentication to satisfy EU strong customer authentication rules.
articles.tieback: As banks start running live agent-initiated transactions over existing card rails, the merchants on the other end need clean, real-time product and order data or the agent has nothing trustworthy to transact against, which is the gap Logicbroker's automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility close.

articles.title: Ambi Robotics and Pickle Robot Integrate AI-Powered Robots to Automate Inbound Warehouse Logistics
articles.author: Sam Francis
articles.summary: Ambi Robotics and Pickle Robot integrated their AI-powered robotic systems into a single inbound logistics workflow that unloads trailers and stacks pallets with minimal human intervention, built in response to demand from Fortune 500 retailers. The companies say the combined system runs inside existing warehouse infrastructure without requiring facility redesigns.
articles.tieback: Automating the physical unload-to-shelf handoff only pays off if the order and inventory data behind it updates in real time, the same visibility gap Logicbroker closes for dropship and 3P suppliers feeding those warehouses.

articles.title: Albertsons Works to Scale Merchandising Intelligence Platform
articles.publisher: Grocery Dive (first published by CIO Dive)
articles.author: Makenzie Holland
articles.summary: Albertsons is rolling out an AI-first merchandising intelligence platform built on Databricks, giving merchants a single natural-language interface to query pricing, promotion and assortment data instead of working across fragmented systems. The grocer plans full deployment by the end of 2026, with governance layered in through Databricks' Unity Catalog and AI Gateway.
articles.tieback: The project is really a data-consolidation problem wearing an AI label; Logicbroker's supplier analytics and intelligent routing already solve that consolidation on the vendor and inventory side before the data ever reaches a merchandising tool.

articles.title: Grocers Are Quickly Embracing AI, Research Shows
articles.author: Sam Silverstein
articles.summary: FMI's 2026 industry survey found 68% of food retailers now use AI in their business, up from 47% a year ago, with generative AI usage climbing to 59% and organization-wide GenAI tool adoption more than doubling. Retailers are increasing tech spending even as they stay cautious about how much staff AI will actually let them reassign.
articles.tieback: Rising AI budgets are chasing efficiency gains that stall without clean upstream data; automated EDI and fast SKU onboarding are the kind of foundational fix that keeps those AI investments from hitting a data-quality ceiling.

articles.title: Companies Trust AI's Advice but Not Its Actions
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence survey of senior technology executives found that nearly every wholesale firm and 90% of retailers currently restrict AI agents to look-up access only, letting them retrieve information but not act autonomously, even though most of the same firms name semi-autonomous AI as their five-year goal. The gap points to a governance and trust problem rather than a technology limitation.
articles.tieback: Retailers eager for semi-autonomous AI still won't grant it execution rights, which is exactly why a transactionable, auditable presence for AI agents and real-time data feeds will matter more than raw model capability going forward.

articles.title: How Salesforce is positioning itself in the agentic AI landscape
articles.summary: Salesforce framed its latest ecommerce release, including the general availability of Cimulate product discovery technology and a new Storefront Next front end, as its biggest agentic commerce push yet. The release also deepens integrations with OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol and Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, letting merchants surface catalogs directly inside ChatGPT and Gemini.
articles.tieback: As Salesforce pipes retailer catalogs into ChatGPT and Gemini through ACP and UCP, the backend data feeding those protocols has to be clean and current or the connection is worthless, which is exactly the automated EDI and real-time inventory visibility problem Logicbroker solves upstream.

articles.title: Batteries Plus' modernization journey prepared it for agentic AI
articles.author: Abbas Haleem
articles.summary: Batteries Plus spent years building what it calls an AI-Ready Enterprise Architecture to future-proof its tech stack, not knowing it would become the foundation for its current agentic AI tools. The retailer has since cut failed product searches by 25% and now contains 35-40% of customer service inquiries through automation, with propensity modeling planned next.
articles.tieback: Batteries Plus only got agentic AI results because it fixed its data foundation first, the same precondition rapid vendor onboarding and automated EDI create for dropship and 3P suppliers before any agent can act reliably on their catalog.

articles.title: Brookshire Brothers rolls out AI tool for planning promotions
articles.author: Catherine Douglas Moran
articles.summary: Grocery chain Brookshire Brothers completed its rollout of Cognira's PromoAI, giving the employee-owned, 100-plus-store retailer a single platform to plan, forecast, and evaluate promotions across departments. The tool is meant to cut manual planning inefficiencies and give teams a clearer read on promotional ROI after each event.
articles.tieback: Promotion forecasting is only as good as the inventory and supplier data behind it, which is why real-time order and inventory visibility matters as much as the forecasting model itself when a retailer is deciding what to discount and when.

articles.title: Scotts Miracle-Gro widens tech partnership for supply chain AI
articles.author: Antone Gonsalves
articles.summary: Scotts Miracle-Gro is expanding its partnership with planning software provider Kinaxis to unify demand planning, decision-making, and execution onto a single AI-assisted platform. The company expects the move to improve responsiveness and resilience across its lawn-care and fertilizer supply chain.
articles.tieback: Unified planning-to-execution platforms like this only perform as well as the order and inventory signals feeding them, which is the operational layer Logicbroker's intelligent routing and supplier analytics provide across a dropship or 3P vendor network.

articles.title: Why AI Shopping Won't Disrupt Every Retail Category Equally
articles.author: Michelle Evans
articles.summary: Forbes retail analyst Michelle Evans argues retailers should assess AI shopping disruption category by category rather than apply one blanket strategy, since some categories benefit far more from AI's ability to cut shopper uncertainty and comparison effort than others.
articles.tieback: Category-level AI readiness comes down to whether a retailer's product and inventory data in that category is current and structured, which is the SKU onboarding speed and catalog data quality question that determines which categories actually show up well in agentic discovery.

articles.title: Agentic Payments Give CFOs Usage Pricing With Subscription Discipline
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: PYMNTS covers Cloudflare's new Monetization Gateway and the x402 payment protocol, which lets systems charge for API calls, data pulls and other machine-triggered requests using the long-unused HTTP 402 status code. The piece argues the nearer-term opportunity for agentic AI isn't consumer shopping but enterprise back-office transactions, where CFOs will want batch settlement, spending limits and audit trails rather than a stream of one-off micropayments.
articles.tieback: The reconciliation problem PYMNTS describes, tracking which workflow, vendor and cost center a machine-triggered transaction belongs to, is the same problem Logicbroker's automated EDI already solves for supplier order and invoice data today.

articles.title: Are grocers making smart investments in back-end AI?
articles.author: Jeff Wells
articles.summary: Grocery Dive details how grocers like Hy-Vee, Grocery Outlet and Albertsons are getting more value from back-end AI on forecasting, replenishment and quality inspection than from consumer-facing chatbots, but sources warn that fragmented, disconnected data undercuts the payoff. Experts say moving toward agentic retailing requires a connected "data fabric" spanning inventory, vendor and store systems before AI can make reliable autonomous decisions.
articles.tieback: This is the gap Logicbroker closes for dropship and 3P networks: real-time order and inventory visibility across suppliers gives back-end AI the connected data it needs, instead of the siloed vendor data the article describes as holding grocers back.

articles.title: Retailers plan to invest deeper in AI, cybersecurity this year
articles.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris
articles.summary: A KPMG survey of 250 retail executives found 52% of retailers now spend $50 million or more a year on technology, with AI and agentic AI among the top areas for planned spending increases. Just 42% of respondents say they're deploying AI at scale today, though 74% expect to reach that point within 12 months.
articles.tieback: Retailers scaling that AI budget still need current supplier and inventory data underneath it, which is exactly what automated EDI and real-time inventory visibility are built to provide.

articles.title: The Mess Most Companies Call An AI Strategy
articles.author: David Van Ronk
articles.summary: Van Ronk argues most companies confuse a pile of AI tools and pilots with an actual strategy, noting that teams forget why past decisions were made and end up re-litigating the same choices. He frames a real AI strategy as a documented, living record of reasoning rather than a static plan filed away after a kickoff meeting.
articles.tieback: This is a useful gut check for prospects: a platform decision like automated EDI or real-time supplier visibility needs documented reasoning up front, or the same vendor onboarding debate resurfaces every time leadership changes.

articles.title: How AI Is Redefining Business Planning
articles.author: Tom Strohl
articles.summary: Strohl writes that AI is compressing planning cycles that once took a month into a matter of days, letting leaders spend less time assembling data and more time acting on it. The piece frames this as a shift in what planning teams are for, less data wrangling, more judgment calls on what to do with a faster stream of insight.
articles.tieback: That shift only holds up if the underlying operational data, like vendor order status and inventory position, is current, which is the layer real-time inventory and order visibility is meant to keep accurate.

articles.title: As AI Agents Transform Commerce, Salesforce Unleashes Its Biggest Agentforce Commerce Release Yet
articles.summary: Salesforce made its Shopper Agent, Buyer Agent, and Merchant Agent generally available, with native integration into ChatGPT now live and Google Search and Gemini integrations coming soon. The release ties agent-led shopping directly to a retailer's own catalog, inventory, and order data rather than treating AI as a bolt-on chatbot.
articles.tieback: Salesforce is betting that agent-native commerce still lives or dies on real-time inventory and order data behind the scenes, the same order and inventory visibility gap Logicbroker closes for retailers connecting to dropship and 3P suppliers.

articles.title: A Tale of Two Amazon Prime Days
articles.author: Dan Berthiaume
articles.summary: Amazon's June 2026 Prime Day grew total U.S. online spend 9.3% year over year to $26.4 billion, but average order size and household spend both slipped versus 2025. AI-driven traffic to retail sites rose 89% year over year during the event and converted 40% better than traffic from other channels.
articles.tieback: AI-referred traffic converting well above other channels is a preview of what agent-driven order volume will demand from a retailer's backend: real-time order and inventory visibility across suppliers so those conversions don't turn into stockouts or delayed fulfillment.

articles.title: Why ERP Isn't Just Another Platform You Can Rebuild With AI Code
articles.author: Chris Lloyd
articles.summary: The piece argues manufacturers shouldn't try to rebuild core ERP systems with AI-generated ("vibe coded") software, citing a finding that 45% of AI-generated code contains security flaws. It recommends applying AI to narrow, well-specified tasks like document processing and shop floor visibility rather than replacing systems of record.
articles.tieback: The caution against DIY AI rebuilds of core systems supports the case for platforms with proven, automated EDI and integration logic already built in, rather than asking internal teams to stitch together fragile custom code for vendor onboarding and order routing.

articles.title: When Developing an AI Strategy, Beware the Urgency Trap
articles.author: David De Cremer
articles.summary: De Cremer cites survey data showing roughly 90% of executives report no measurable productivity gain from AI over the past three years, arguing that framing AI as a fix for urgent bottlenecks causes initiatives to start fast but fail to deliver lasting value. He recommends leaders prioritize clarity of purpose over urgency when building an AI strategy.
articles.tieback: The "urgency trap" shows up in retail tech buying too: chasing a quick AI fix for onboarding or fulfillment pain without addressing the underlying supplier connectivity and data problems that rapid vendor onboarding and intelligent routing are built to solve properly.

articles.title: Amazon offers agentic shoppers up to 365 days of price history
articles.summary: Amazon expanded its Alexa for Shopping assistant to show 30, 90, and 365 days of price history directly on product pages, alongside existing agentic features like auto-buying at a target price. The rollout continues Amazon's push to have its AI shopping layer handle more of the buying decision, not just product discovery.
articles.tieback: For dropship and 3P sellers, this raises the bar on how fast and accurately supplier pricing and inventory data needs to sync back to marketplace listings, since stale price or stock data now gets surfaced directly to AI-assisted shoppers.

articles.title: Adyen on Agentic Commerce: The AI Was Never the Hard Part
articles.summary: Adyen's global head of agentic commerce, Karan Katyal, told PYMNTS the industry sits at 0.5 on a five-point maturity scale and will roughly triple activity in the next year. He said the real bottleneck isn't the AI itself but the infrastructure underneath it: machine-readable product catalogs, fragmented protocols, and unresolved questions about fraud and liability when an agent transacts on a shopper's behalf.
articles.tieback: The catalog and trust gap Katyal describes is exactly where automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility matter most, since an agent can't transact against a supplier's product data if that data isn't structured, current, and machine-readable in the first place.

articles.title: How AI Erased a $184 Billion Supply Chain Blind Spot
articles.summary: C.H. Robinson's new Lean AI Engineer tool assesses an entire supply chain in under 30 minutes and acts on inefficiencies in real time, replacing a process that used to take four weeks of backward-looking analysis. Annual supply chain disruption costs of $184 billion are driven less by the disruptions themselves than by the lag between spotting a problem and acting on it.
articles.tieback: This is the same lag that real-time order and inventory visibility plus intelligent routing and supplier analytics are built to close, turning weeks of backward-looking reporting into an operational feed suppliers and retailers can act on immediately.

articles.title: The top supply chain stress sources include…
articles.summary: A new Inspectorio survey of nearly 200 supply chain professionals found compliance strain rising while budgets flatten, with only 21% of organizations having a multi-tier traceability strategy. Inspectorio's CEO said the biggest obstacle to effective AI adoption isn't the technology, it's insufficient data quality, change management gaps, and lack of cross-functional integration.
articles.tieback: That data quality bottleneck is a direct argument for rapid, standardized vendor onboarding and automated EDI, since AI initiatives stall when supplier and compliance data arrives fragmented or in inconsistent formats.

articles.title: AI Is Changing How Customers Choose Your Business
articles.author: Graham Kenny and Ganna Pogrebna
articles.summary: Graham Kenny and Ganna Pogrebna argue that as AI increasingly mediates how business customers research and choose suppliers, competitive advantage is shifting from direct customer understanding to managing how AI systems represent a company. They cite three companies that adapted by screening AI-generated inquiries, monitoring how AI tools describe their business, and replacing periodic reviews with continuous monitoring of AI-generated market perceptions.
articles.tieback: For B2B sellers on marketplaces, this reinforces the case for a transactionable presence on LLMs and agents, since suppliers not structured for AI-mediated discovery risk being screened out before a buyer ever sees their catalog.

articles.title: Visa Payments Forum in Paris: Agentic Commerce is Coming
articles.author: Natalia Elliot
articles.summary: At its Payments Forum in Paris, Visa announced that AI agents can now search, select, and initiate purchases on merchant websites across Europe using its Intelligent Commerce infrastructure, working with 30 European issuers and merchants including lastminute.com and Frasers. Visa also expanded Visa Agentic Ready to merchants through a new Trusted Agent Protocol and Agent Directory, and said the same model will extend to B2B payment scenarios.
articles.tieback: As payment networks build the rails for agents to transact directly with individual merchants, suppliers whose product, price, and inventory data isn't clean and real-time will be invisible to the agent at the exact moment it's ready to buy.

articles.title: Square Intros ChatGPT and Claude Integrations for Sellers
articles.summary: Square launched a ChatGPT app and Claude plugin that let merchants get discovered and take orders directly inside AI conversations, starting with food and beverage sellers on Square Online Ordering, with automatic enrollment and no added fees. Square is also extending AI-powered discovery to voice commerce through a partnership with Amazon's Alexa+.
articles.tieback: Square's zero-setup approach lowers the bar for showing up inside agent conversations, raising the stakes for suppliers that still can't connect accurate inventory and order data fast enough to participate.

articles.title: Brands focus agentic AI on lower-level customer experience workflows
articles.summary: An Infobip 2026 Customer Experience Maturity Report found 53% of global brands have adopted agentic AI for lower-value tasks like feedback collection and reminders, but adoption drops sharply for higher-value workflows such as loyalty management (35%), delivery management (28%), and returns and refunds (15%). Infobip's chief revenue officer attributes the gap to fragmented systems rather than a lack of appetite for deeper automation.
articles.tieback: The steep drop-off in agentic AI adoption for delivery management and returns tracks directly to fragmented order and inventory data, the gap that real-time order and inventory visibility is built to close.

articles.title: Amazon invests $1 billion to embed AI engineers with clients
articles.summary: AWS is committing $1 billion to a new Forward Deployed Engineering unit that embeds engineering teams directly inside customer organizations to build and deploy production agentic AI systems in weeks rather than months. Amazon frames it as a break from traditional consulting, with customers left owning both the finished system and the in-house skills to extend it.
articles.tieback: As cloud providers race to shrink the time between deciding to deploy AI and having it live in production, the retailers who benefit most will be the ones whose supplier and inventory data is already clean enough for an embedded engineering team to build on.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: The top CPG retailer fulfillment pain points are...
articles.summary: A Dynata survey of 50 CPG retail executives conducted for Radial found 48% cite technology integrations and data visibility as their top fulfillment pain point, ahead of e-commerce fulfillment speed (38%) and routing guide compliance and chargebacks (30%). Two-thirds of respondents said it's highly important that a single 3PL partner handle both retail replenishment and e-commerce fulfillment, and 30% named EDI integration a required 3PL capability.
articles.tieback: Technology integration and data visibility topping the pain point list is a direct match for what automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility are built to fix in a CPG-heavy fulfillment conversation.

articles.title: Inside AI's $5 trillion quest to give agentic AI a sense of taste
articles.author: Elizabeth Segran
articles.summary: Shopping agents from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic can browse and compare products but still struggle to match people with brands that fit their taste, since large language models lack the aesthetic judgment behind most real purchase decisions. The piece traces the plumbing being built for agentic commerce, including OpenAI and Stripe's Agentic Commerce Protocol and Google and Shopify's Universal Commerce Protocol, and notes that checkout inside AI chat still stumbles on inventory and personalization gaps.
articles.tieback: Agentic checkout only works if the AI can see accurate, real-time product and inventory data, the same data layer Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility and transactionable LLM presence are built to supply.

articles.title: Square launches agentic commerce integrations with ChatGPT, Claude
articles.summary: Square rolled out a ChatGPT app and a Claude plugin that let food and beverage sellers on Square Online Ordering get discovered and take orders directly inside those AI assistants, with no new contracts or marketplace commissions beyond standard processing fees. Square is also joining the AAIF Agentic Commerce Working Group and partnering with Google on the Universal Commerce Protocol for local ordering and delivery.
articles.tieback: AI assistants are becoming a real order channel that small and mid-size merchants need to plug into, the same transactionable presence on LLMs and agents that Logicbroker is building toward for its supplier network.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: The top CPG retailer fulfillment pain points are...
articles.summary: A Dynata survey of 50 CPG retail executives, commissioned by Radial, found that 48% cite technology integrations and data visibility as their top fulfillment pain point, ahead of DTC fulfillment speed (38%) and routing guide compliance and chargebacks (30%). More than half of respondents also said their 3PL needs to integrate with Salesforce, SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Amazon Seller/Vendor Central and Shopify, while only 30% flagged EDI integration specifically.
articles.tieback: Technology integration gaps and routing guide chargebacks are exactly what automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility are built to eliminate, making this survey a direct read on the pain Logicbroker sells against.

articles.title: Digital twins, software maturity lead manufacturing automation trends
articles.author: Nathan Owens and Katie Pyzyk
articles.summary: At the Automate conference, speakers described engineers using large language models through an MCP-style agent interface to pull technical specs and quotes for faster, smarter robot simulation. They also warned that AI still requires per-process configuration and that finance teams want quality and risk cases, not headcount savings, before greenlighting automation spend.
articles.tieback: The same MCP-style pattern that lets an AI agent pull structured technical data on demand is the model Logicbroker applies to supplier analytics and intelligent routing across a dropship network.

articles.title: 4 experts on how to make AI investments worthwhile
articles.author: Bryan Wassel
articles.summary: Leaders at Customer Contact Week Las Vegas warned that AI vendors often oversell capabilities that add friction instead of value, and urged buyers to understand the true cost to scale before signing on and to judge vendors on long-term reliability rather than a polished demo. They also stressed that any AI rollout has to start from what customers actually want, not from what the technology can technically do.
articles.tieback: The advice to weigh a vendor's long-term reliability and real cost to scale over a slick demo is a useful lens for retailers evaluating any AI-driven commerce platform, including one built for dropship and marketplace onboarding.
